parsed.title: Internal-step count bumped to 19 but the enumerated list still totals 18
parsed.detail: The header now says "**19 internal steps**" and the parenthetical enumerates: 2 planning steps + 2 evidence owners + review-implementation + planning-preflight + phase-contract + verification-contract + 9-skill review pack = 2+2+1+1+1+1+9 = 17, plus the newly added `replan-findings` row = 18. The `replan-findings` row was added to the table but the count arithmetic in the intro paragraph was not reconciled with the enumerated set; the same mismatch appears in SKILLS.es.md ("19 pasos internos").

parsed.title: `fix-now / replan-in-unit` bullet conflates two distinct classes and routes fix-now through the replan router
parsed.detail: The bullet is headed "**fix-now / replan-in-unit** → run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`" but the immediately preceding bullet already says fix-now "folds directly into the current unit's open phase. Never a tracked issue, never `plan-fix` (AC 12)." Routing fix-now through the replan router (which names `/plan-feature` or `/plan-fix`) directly contradicts AC 12's "never `plan-fix`" and the fix-now fold contract. The same conflation is in REVIEW_AND_CLASSIFY.es.md line 88.

parsed.title: Router invocation documented as `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` but the router is described elsewhere as a script that emits a typed route from ledger/read-set
parsed.detail: The doc claims the router's `route: replan` line "names the planner (`/plan-feature` for a feature, `/plan-fix` for a fix)". The unit's own fix-index row (docs/fix/README.md #224) describes the router as emitting "a typed route" and "a bounded read set" — not a planner name. If the router emits a route token (e.g. `replan`) rather than a planner name, the doc's claim that the line "names the planner" is unsupported by the described contract; the reader is told to read a planner name out of a line the router is not documented to produce.

parsed.title: `replan-in-unit` now requires running a script and a fresh `/review-plan` but the surrounding prose still frames it as a direct SPEC append
parsed.detail: The diff replaces "`replan-in-unit` appends new user-confirmed phases to the unit's SPEC" with "`replan-in-unit` runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`, whose `route: replan` line names the planner that appends new user-confirmed phases to the unit's SPEC (fresh `/review-plan` first)". The same paragraph's other classes (fix-now, decision-required, proposals) remain single-step prose; only replan-in-unit now requires a script invocation plus a review gate. The doc does not state what happens when the router prints a non-`replan` route (e.g. `fix-now` or `decision-required`) for a finding classified replan-in-unit — the reader is left with an invocation that may not produce the named line. Same gap in FEATURE_WORKFLOW.es.md line 319.

parsed.title: Portable prompt hardcodes `node scripts/unit-route.mjs` into a project-agnostic bootstrap prompt
parsed.detail: The portable prompt's stated contract is to "regenerate the agentic workflow ... **adapted to that project's** architecture, documentation, and conventions, rather than copying this repo's specifics verbatim" and to "degrade gracefully and say so at runtime rather than assuming a path" when something doesn't exist. The new text hardcodes `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` — a path that exists only in this repo — into the prompt that is pasted into arbitrary target repositories. A target repo without that script gets a documented invocation that fails. Same issue in PORTABLE_PROMPT.es.md line 147.

parsed.title: `replan-findings` row claims it is "composed by `plan-feature` / `plan-fix`" but the router is invoked from review, not from the planners
parsed.detail: The new row says `replan-findings` is "`user-invocable: false` — composed by `plan-feature` / `plan-fix` on that route". But the router `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` is documented in REVIEW_AND_CLASSIFY.md and FEATURE_WORKFLOW.md as being run by the reviewer/fold path (the `replan-in-unit` destination), not by `plan-feature`/`plan-fix`. The planner is the destination the router names, not the caller that composes `replan-findings`. The composition claim contradicts the invocation path documented in the same slice. Same in SKILLS.es.md line 111.

parsed.title: Fix #224 row marked `done` while the unit's own slice is still under review
parsed.detail: The row status is `done · [#225](...)` and the legend says `done` means "built, PR open, awaiting merge". The unit being reviewed is `fix/224-deterministic-replan-routing` with a pending change slice ("tutorial-crossrefs") still under review — the row is being added in the same slice that is not yet merged. Per the legend the row is removed only after merge, but marking `done` before the review passes contradicts the unit's own recorded state (the slice is pending review, not built-and-awaiting-merge).
